reports.authors: Wenzel C; Walzik D; Wences T; Trebing S; Meyer K; Groll A; Zimmer P; Joisten N
reports.version_date: Accepted 14 October 2025 (masthead: Received 10 Sep 2025; Revised 13 Oct 2025; Accepted 14 Oct 2025); Acta Physiologica 2025;241:e70125.
reports.version_label: version of record; article type 'Did You Know?' (open-access short communication/research letter, not a full-length original article)
source_locator: p.4 Author Contributions/Conflicts of Interest/Data Availability/References/Supporting Information
reports.inclusion_reason: Single identifiable 40-min acute aerobic exercise bout at 60% VO2peak with a pre-exercise baseline and dense within-bout/recovery venous sampling (baseline, warm-up, 10/15/30/40 min, 1h post), all within the 0-72h organising window; targeted immunological protein panel (Olink 96 Immuno-Oncology) measured in 12 healthy adults satisfies the immune-linkage rule as recognized_immune_mediator. Meets Core A per contract 2.1-2.2 (p.1).
reports.reviewer_notes: AI stand-in for reviewer C, 10-report charting pilot only (C uses the '_B' screening slot; reviewer_A left null). This is a 4-page Wiley 'Did You Know?' open-access research letter/short communication, not a full-length original article: it has no separate headed Methods/Results/Discussion sections, states the ethics committee by name only (no approval number given), and omits some details a full Methods section would normally state explicitly (exact blood matrix, exercise modality/ergometer). See unresolved_questions.
reports.author_stated_use: NR - no explicit statement of an intended downstream clinical/monitoring application was found; the Discussion (p.3) is framed entirely around mechanistic kinetic characterization and exercise-duration dependence of protein responses, not a stated use case.
author_window_interpretation_locator: Full text (p.1-3) reviewed; no use of 'open window', 'immunosuppression', 'susceptibility' or 'redistribution' framing anywhere. Discussion (p.3) frames findings only in terms of protein kinetics/clustering and exercise-duration dependence, e.g. 'a longer exercise duration seems to promote stronger and more distinct immunological adaptations' (p.3).

measurements.platform: Olink (R) 96 Immuno-Oncology Panel, proximity extension assay (PEA); output = NPX values (p.1)
measurements.cell_context: NA (cell-free plasma/serum protein assay; exact matrix UNCLEAR, see sample_sets.matrix)
measurements.assay_validity: Olink PEA internal QC (not itemized in this 4-page letter); 92 of 96 panel proteins produced quantifiable NPX output (4 not quantified/not stated why) (p.1).
measurements.comparison: Linear mixed model (LMM) for each of the 92 proteins across 7 timepoints vs baseline, with time point and sex as fixed effects and subject ID as a random effect; Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p<0.05 and >=1 significant time coefficient required for 'significant' classification (p.1).
measurements.effect_measure: LMM fixed-effect estimate per timepoint vs baseline (on NPX, a log2-like scale)
measurements.effect_uncertainty: Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p<0.05 threshold, >=1 significant time coefficient required
measurements.multiplicity: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across the 92 tested proteins and their time coefficients
measurements.confounding: Sex included as a fixed effect in the same LMM as time; no other confounders (diet beyond the overnight fast, sleep, menstrual-cycle phase, prior training) are reported as measured or adjusted for.
measurements.donor_level_inference: Subject ID modeled as a random effect; statistical unit = participant (n=12) across all 7 repeated timepoints.
measurements.null_findings: 48 of 92 proteins (52%) did not reach the significance threshold at any timepoint (i.e. did not show >=1 significant time coefficient); these are named in Supplement Table S1 sheet 'Proteins' and have full per-timepoint statistics in sheet 'LMM_results', but are not individually itemized as separate measurement rows in this pilot pass (see unresolved_questions).
measurements.reported_feature_count: 44 of 92 proteins (48%) showed significant time-dependent change (p.1, p.3); grouped into 4 hierarchical-clustering patterns (Figure 1D).
measurements.measurement_notes: Assay-level summary for the full targeted Olink Immuno-Oncology panel. tested_universe_n=92 is the number of proteins with quantifiable NPX output out of the 96-protein commercial panel (4 presumably below detection or QC-failed; the letter does not explain the 96->92 reduction). Named-candidate rows below cover all 44 proteins reported as significant by the LMM (Figure 1D cluster assignment + exact LMM estimate/p-value for the single strongest timepoint, transcribed from Supplement Table S1 sheet 'LMM_results'); the 48 non-significant proteins are not individually itemized as rows here (row-volume judgement call, consistent with the treatment of R61's non-exhaustive GSEA table).

precision_validation.replication: No explicit assay-level reliability statistic (CV, LOD, inter-plate/inter-assay concordance) is reported for the Olink panel in this 4-page letter; standard Olink QC procedures are not described in the accessible text.
precision_validation.evidence_notes: The short research-letter format omits a conventional Methods section; no CV/LOD/QC-failure-rate data for the 92 quantified proteins is given. Marker family in play: cytokine_or_inflammatory_mediator (plus several non-cytokine analytes, see unresolved_questions).

precision_validation.response_evidence: Dense within-bout and recovery sampling: baseline, warm-up, 10/15/30/40 min (during/end of the 40-min bout) and 1h post; all within the organising window (during_exercise_ancillary through 30min_to_lt3h bins).
precision_validation.evidence_notes: This is the report's strongest domain: 7 timepoints densely sampled within a single bout and short recovery window, explicitly motivated by the authors as filling a gap in 'high-resolution examination of the kinetic changes during exercise itself' (p.1). No sampling beyond 1h post, so longer-recovery (24-72h) kinetics are not charted.

precision_validation.individualization: t-SNE analysis shows distinct clusters for each individual and separation by sex (Figure 1B, p.1), described by the authors as evidence that 'immune responses to acute exercise are highly individual and influenced by sex'. However this is a single exercise session per participant with no repeated baseline or repeated-bout design, so inter-individual differences are observed but not quantified as reproducible (no ICC/CV/responder-consistency statistic across sessions).
precision_validation.evidence_notes: Per the extraction manual's default rule, a single pre-post (here, single-session multi-timepoint) dataset without repeated-baseline/repeat-bout data cannot be called a validated individualized marker, even though qualitative inter-individual/sex heterogeneity is explicitly reported.

precision_validation.functional_evidence: No direct immune-function assay (e.g. actual NK cytotoxicity, phagocytosis, stimulated-cytokine release) was performed; the paper infers NK-cell activity from granzyme protein kinetics by citing external literature on NK-cell behaviour (ref. 9), not by measuring function directly in this cohort.
precision_validation.evidence_notes: Correlation-network (Fig. 1E) and SHAP/random-forest (Fig. 1F) analyses relate different proteins' AUCs to each other (e.g. other proteins predicting IL-10 at 1h post) - this is a co-measured statistical association between biomarkers, not a function test or a clinical/infection outcome. No clinical endpoint of any kind is reported.

precision_validation.replication: A random forest model (predicting 1h-post IL-10 from exercise-phase protein AUCs) was validated by leave-one-out cross-validation within the same 12 participants (p.3 Figure 1 legend: 'Model validation was conducted using the leave-one-out method'). This is internal resampling of the same cohort, not an independent cohort or external dataset.
precision_validation.prediction_design: Random forest model per protein concentration at 1h post exercise, trained on 44 LMM-significant protein AUCs during exercise; target variable unscaled, features z-transformed; hyperparameters tuned by Bayesian search (p.3 Figure 1 legend).
precision_validation.prediction_metrics: Root mean square error (RMSE) reported as the model-quality metric (p.3 Figure 1 legend); no discrimination/calibration/sensitivity-specificity metrics, since the target is continuous (IL-10 concentration), not a classification endpoint.
precision_validation.leakage_control: Leave-one-out cross-validation is a form of participant-level resampling within one cohort, not a held-out independent test set; hyperparameter search procedure vs. feature-selection-leakage control is not explicitly described.
precision_validation.evidence_notes: Per vocabulary_crosswalks.evidence_state, only independent_site_or_cohort validation supports evidence_present for this domain; leave-one-out on the same 12 participants is resampling_same_participants, which maps to not_demonstrated.

study_families.design: Single-arm, fully repeated-measures (within-subject) acute exercise trial: 7 venous blood timepoints (baseline through 1h post) around one 40-min aerobic bout; no non-exercise control arm; linear mixed models with subject ID as random effect.
study_families.cointerventions: Overnight fast before the morning exercise session (8-10 AM start) (p.1).
study_families.study_notes: Data portal named 'Immune signature and exercise' hosted at https://sportsmedicine-dortmund.shinyapps.io/beat (p.1, p.4 Data Availability), informally referred to here as 'BEAT'. Reference 6 in this report (Kurgan, Kjaergaard, Jespersen et al., 'Body Fluid Proteomic Landscape of Acute Exercise', bioRxiv 2025, DOI 10.1101/2025.05.28.656705) is cited for sex-related individual variability in exercise protein responses and may originate from an overlapping research network/data portal, but authorship does not overlap with this report and the text does not state whether participants overlap. Whether this n=12 cohort is shared with any other pilot report or with the Kurgan et al. preprint cannot be determined from this report's text alone; flagged for human cross-report adjudication (this report's own pilot_purpose explicitly names 'shared cohort' as the calibration target).

eligibility_opinion.rationale: Single identifiable 40-min acute aerobic exercise bout at 60% VO2peak with a pre-exercise baseline and dense within-bout/recovery venous sampling through 1h post (p.1), entirely within the 0-72h organising window and with no exposure threshold required (contract 2.1-2.2). A targeted immunological protein panel (Olink 96 Immuno-Oncology: cytokines, chemokines, effector molecules, cell-surface markers; p.1) measured in 12 healthy adults satisfies the immune-linkage rule as recognized_immune_mediator.

unresolved_questions: Blood matrix (plasma vs serum) is never explicitly named in the accessible 4-page text; 'venous blood samples were collected... and processed immediately after collection' (p.1) does not specify the final analyte matrix for the Olink assay. Recorded as UNCLEAR in sample_sets.matrix; the manual should state whether reviewers may infer a platform's typical default matrix (Olink PEA is commonly run on plasma) or must always mark UNCLEAR absent an explicit statement.

Exercise modality (cycling vs treadmill/other ergometer) is likewise never explicitly named; only '40-min aerobic exercise session at 60% of their VO2peak' is given (p.1), and the Figure 1A icon is not machine-readable text. Recorded sample_sets.exercise_mode as UNCLEAR.

Shared-cohort question (this report's own pilot_purpose explicitly names this as the calibration target): reference 6 (Kurgan et al. 2025 bioRxiv, 'Body Fluid Proteomic Landscape of Acute Exercise') and this report share the same TU Dortmund Sports Medicine research context and a similarly named online data portal, but authors do not overlap and the text does not state whether participants/cohorts overlap. The manual does not specify how much circumstantial similarity (institution, topic, dashboard naming) should trigger a mandatory cross-report cohort-identity check versus being left to study_notes as a flag for human adjudication.

Row-volume policy for large targeted-panel omics (92 quantified Olink proteins, 737-row full LMM supplement table): this pilot created 1 assay-universe row + 44 named-candidate rows (one per significant protein, using the single strongest of up to 6 timepoint-level LMM coefficients per protein) rather than fully enumerating all 92 proteins x 7 timepoints (=644 potential rows) or all 48 non-significant proteins individually. The manual should state explicitly whether full timepoint-level enumeration is required for dense repeated-measures kinetic designs, or whether a 'strongest timepoint' summary per named candidate (as done here) is an acceptable extraction unit.

marker_family assignment required subjective judgement for several Olink Immuno-Oncology analytes that are not classic leukocyte/cytokine markers (e.g. growth factors FGF2, PDGF-B, EGF, VEGFA, VEGFR-2, ANGPT2; tumour marker CAIX; costimulatory receptors CD40/CD40-L/TWEAK/TNFSF14); these were coded 'other' by default, which is defensible but not rule-driven, and may understate immune-specific family counts in downstream figures.

This report's publication format is a 4-page Wiley 'Did You Know?' short communication/research letter without separate headed Methods/Results/Discussion sections, an explicit ethics-approval number, or some standard methodological details (see above). The manual does not currently distinguish full-length original articles from short-communication formats for completeness expectations; flagging this format difference as a possible source of systematic NR/UNCLEAR rates across pilot reports.
